Docs/Replay/Guide

Replay

Native authenticated two-player P2P

2 min readOdin × GodotPage source ↓

P2P_Direct manages an ENet connection between two participants enrolled through P2P_Party. It discovers the peer's registered endpoint, requests a scoped pair key, authenticates the physical connection and exposes stable member IDs through transport.Transport. It replaces failed transports without owning or rewinding the gameplay runner. The application retains and rebinds that runner as described below.

  1. Open/pump P2P_Party with native Party_Storage, verified service TLS and a native endpoint. The endpoint is re-registered each process, while the original persisted enrollment request remains unchanged for exact retries.
  2. Once Party is ready, call p2p_direct_open. The first member listens; the other queries the service before connecting. This convenience owner supports exactly two members. Other topologies can use the lower-level pair/link APIs. An optional P2P_Direct_Options.listen selects the local bind address/port independently of the advertised Party endpoint. Empty options retain the existing behavior. The options are copied, and the advertised endpoint is never rewritten from the bind configuration.
  3. Give p2p_direct_transport to the game's transport wrappers/runner. Continue pumping p2p_party_frame once per frame before polling gameplay. Registration and pair-key messages use separate Router lanes on the same control socket.
  4. Read p2p_direct_identity only after admission. The transport uses the remote member ID, not the ENet ID. generation is a monotone authenticated connection serial even when a reopened ENet owner reuses an ID.
  5. On a new admitted generation, rebind the retained P2P runner. A fresh returning process restores a compatible participant archive; credentials contain no simulation/input history. Close the gameplay transport before closing Party.

Pair requests are made for the current connection. A missing remote registration or rate-limit result retries after 500 ms. ENet connection/cryptographic handshakes have five-second attempt bounds. Failed links are retired; replacements use fresh pair decisions and cryptographic nonces. Newer signed roster incarnations retire older links. Signed registration refusal clears link keys. An unavailable background control connection does not by itself close an admitted link, but new admission still needs the service.

The listener permits eight pending ENet peers but admits one pair. This is not a DDoS availability guarantee. Use listen for a local interface behind a forwarded advertised address/port. Port forwarding is deployment configuration; this owner does not establish arbitrary NAT traversal. Native/browser gameplay needs a common backend; this ENet owner does not connect directly to browser WebRTC.

See link security/lifetime and pair provisioning. The framing is experimental and has not received independent cryptographic review. Native macOS integration and WASM package checks have run; broader platform validation remains separate.

tests/replay_p2p_native/run.sh covers TLS enrollment, encrypted gameplay, process kills and both return roles. Creator return changes its listen port; the survivor discovers the new signed endpoint and preserves its runner. Game parity is not part of this integration gate.
